lesion.mechanism: disable_recurrent zeroes raw_delta (latent.rs apply_to_delta); plain NCA (carry_channels=0) -> state frozen at token embedding for all 16 ticks; verified state max_dev=0
lesion.query_inputs: all 128 masked positions have input token '?' (verified)
lesion.frozen_logit_structure: 3 distinct logit vectors over all 512 lattice positions (one per distinct input token '0','1','?'); query-site logits identical across all 32 sequences (max_dev=0); NOT constant over entire sequence
lesion.verdict: NOT class inversion and NOT saturation. Every lesion prediction is a single constant token (a pure function of the frozen '?' embedding). Accuracy = base rate of that constant token among targets: 0.0 when the token is not a parity symbol, 0.53125 for B when the token is '0' (== target '0' base rate). The A-vs-B lesion contrast carries no information about learned recurrence.

nan_replay.mechanism_evidence: First nonfinite tensors are recurrent-path gradients while forward state, logits, loss and pre-step params are finite. Premature gradient-norm spikes (up to 125 early, oscillating 2-37 near onset) are NOT a monotone precursor; the fatal step had a finite forward with NaN gradients, so the failure lives in the backward unroll, not an observed forward state explosion.

rd018_forensics_findings.skeptic_alternative: If the original 'lesion proves recurrence necessary / A collapses while B survives' reading is wrong, the data are equally consistent with: the lesion metric is a degenerate constant predictor whose value is fixed by whichever token the frozen '?' readout argmaxes to plus the skewed target prior. It cannot discriminate recurrent computation. Cross-path caveat: rollout/benchmark (nca.rs develop_with_intervention) never calls apply_to_delta, so 'lesion' means different things on the two code paths.
